# `silk/compress/zstd`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Decompress Zstandard data (RFC 8878) in steps, with fixed memory and limits that you set.

## When to use
Use [`Zstd`](#Zstd) to read `.zst` files or HTTP bodies with `Content-Encoding: zstd`. Make a decoder
with [`Zstd.make`](#Zstd.impl.make), and call [`Zstd.step`](#Zstd.impl.step) until it returns `Finished`. This module does not
compress.

## Details
The decoder supports all block types and all entropy modes, and more than one frame, including
skippable frames. [`Zstd.make`](#Zstd.impl.make) allocates all storage one time: the history window, three 128
KiB staging buffers, and the entropy tables. [`Zstd.step`](#Zstd.impl.step) does not allocate and keeps no borrow
of your buffers. The [`ZstdLimits`](#ZstdLimits) apply to the full input, across all frames.

The end of a frame is not the end of the input. The decoder returns `Finished` only when the
input is marked final, all of it is consumed, and each frame is complete.

## Errors
- `OutOfMemoryError` from [`Zstd.make`](#Zstd.impl.make) if the `Allocator` fails.
- [`ZstdError`](#ZstdError) if the configuration is not valid, the data is not valid, a limit is exceeded,
  or the calls do not follow the rules of [`Zstd.step`](#Zstd.impl.step). `reason` gives the cause and `offset`
  the input position.

## Gotchas
Output is not verified until `Finished`, because a checksum or a truncated frame can fail later.
A failure is permanent: drop the decoder and make a new one for another stream. Dictionaries are
not supported.

## Examples
### Decode a frame with one raw block
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.compress.zstd { Zstd, ZstdError, ZstdLimits, ZstdProgress, ZstdStatus }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! ZstdError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut decoder = run Zstd.make(ZstdLimits.make()) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)

  // Magic number, a header for a 2-byte frame, a last raw block of 2 bytes, then "hi".
  let input = b"\x28\xb5\x2f\xfd\x20\x02\x11\x00\x00hi"
  let mut output: [u8; 16] = [0; 16]
  return match Zstd.step(&mut decoder, &input, &mut output, true) {
    Result<ZstdProgress, ZstdError>.Success { value } => {
      if value.status != ZstdStatus.Finished || value.written != 2 || output[0] != 104
        || output[1] != 105 {
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<ZstdProgress, ZstdError>.Failure {..} => 1
  }
}
```

Import as `Zstd` with `import silk.compress.zstd { Zstd }`.

<a id="ZstdLimits.windowBytes"></a>

### Field `windowBytes`

```silk

```

The size of the history buffer that [`Zstd.make`](#Zstd.impl.make) allocates. A frame that asks for a larger
window fails with `WindowLimit`. It must not be 0.

<a id="ZstdLimits.workspaceBytes"></a>

### Field `workspaceBytes`

```silk
pub workspaceBytes: usize
```

The storage budget other than the window: staging buffers, decoder state, and entropy tables.
If it is too small, [`Zstd.make`](#Zstd.impl.make) fails with `WorkspaceLimit`.

Each later call returns the same `reason` and `offset` with no progress. The output that earlier
calls wrote is not valid.

<a id="Zstd"></a>

## `Zstd`

```silk
pub struct Zstd
```

A Zstandard decoder for one complete input. It owns all its storage.

Dropping it releases the storage. Each regular frame starts with a new history, new entropy
tables, and a new checksum, but the limits count across all frames.

### When to use
Use it to read `.zst` files or HTTP bodies with `Content-Encoding: zstd`. Make a decoder with
[`Zstd.make`](#Zstd.impl.make), and call [`Zstd.step`](#Zstd.impl.step) until it returns `Finished`. It does not compress.

### Details
It supports all block types and all entropy modes, and more than one frame, including
skippable frames. [`Zstd.make`](#Zstd.impl.make) allocates all storage one time. [`Zstd.step`](#Zstd.impl.step) does not allocate
and keeps no borrow of your buffers. The end of a frame is not the end of the input: the decoder
returns `Finished` only when the input is marked final, all of it is consumed, and each frame is
complete.

### Gotchas
Output is not verified until `Finished`, because a checksum or a truncated frame can fail later.
A failure is permanent: drop the decoder and make a new one for another stream. Dictionaries are
not supported.

```silk
impl Zstd
```

<a id="Zstd.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(limits: ZstdLimits) -> Self ! ZstdError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a decoder that uses `limits`, with storage from the ambient `Allocator`.

It allocates the window, three 128 KiB staging buffers, and the entropy tables. [`Zstd.step`](#Zstd.impl.step)
does not allocate.

#### Errors
- [`ZstdError`](#ZstdError) with `WorkspaceLimit` if `workspaceBytes` is too small, or with
  `InvalidConfiguration` if `windowBytes` is 0 or the total size does not fit in `usize`.
  These checks come before the allocation.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` fails.

<a id="Zstd.impl.step"></a>

### Method `step`

```silk
pub fn step(self: &mut Self, input: &[u8], output: &mut [u8], finalInput: bool) -> Result<
    ZstdProgress,
    ZstdError,
  >
```

Decodes from `input` into `output` and returns how much it consumed and wrote.

On the next call, give only the input after the consumed prefix, and use only the written
prefix of the output. Set `finalInput` when `input` holds all remaining data. After that, each
call must set `finalInput` and give exactly the input that is not consumed yet. `NeedOutput`
with an empty output makes no progress.

#### Errors
- [`ZstdError`](#ZstdError) if the data is not valid, a [`ZstdLimits`](#ZstdLimits) value would be exceeded, the final
  input ends early (`Truncated`), or the call changes the final input (`InvalidState`).

#### Gotchas
Output is not verified until `Finished`. A failure is permanent for this decoder.
